environment.description: Same application deployed identically but with AWS WAFv2 WebACL associated to the ALB. WebACL contains two rule groups evaluated in order: (1) a custom rule group with a RegexPatternSet rule matching request query string parameters against pattern `(?i)(?:union\s+(?:all\s+)?select|;\s*(?:drop|alter|insert|update|delete|exec)|'\s*(?:or|and)\s+['"]?\w+['"]?\s*[=<>])` with action BLOCK and priority 1, (2) AWS managed rule group AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet with all rules in default action (BLOCK) at priority 2. Additionally, the RDS PostgreSQL instance has the pgaudit extension enabled with pgaudit.log = 'all' and a CloudWatch alarm on query anomalies, and the database connection uses a separate PostgreSQL role 'app_readonly' that has been granted only SELECT on columns (id, username, display_name, department) of the users table via column-level privileges — no SELECT on email, password_hash, or other sensitive columns, and no privileges on other tables including api_keys (the api_keys lookup uses a separate connection pool with a different role 'auth_svc' that has SELECT only on api_keys).

config.wafv2_web_acl: associated to ALB, two rule groups as described
config.custom_regex_rule: blocks common SQL injection patterns in query strings
config.rds_role_app_readonly: GRANT SELECT (id, username, display_name, department) ON users TO app_readonly; no other table access
config.rds_role_auth_svc: GRANT SELECT ON api_keys TO auth_svc; used only for API key verification
config.pgaudit: pgaudit.log = 'all', CloudWatch alarm on anomalous query patterns
config.connection_pools: search endpoint uses app_readonly role, auth decorator uses auth_svc role
